digest.en: Trump floats a Ukraine deal while Rubio defends the Iran strike as necessary. Pope Leo confronts Milei in Argentina, challenging the austerity agenda. Okinawa’s governor demands a review of the US forces pact after a murder.
digest.hi: यमन के बंदरगाह होदेइदाह और सना में दो हफ्ते फँसे 19 भारतीय नाविकों को अंतर्राष्ट्रीय बचाव दल ने सुरक्षित निकाल दिया। इसी दौरान पंजाब में मंत्री कपिल मिश्रा ने दिवाली की रात 1,200 स्थानों पर पराली जलाने का दावा किया, जिससे सुरक्षा चिंताएँ उठीं।

articles.title: Okinawa governor calls for review of US forces pact after murder of Japanese woman
articles.summary: A US Marine was indicted for murdering a 39-year-old Japanese woman in Okinawa. The incident sparked local outrage. The Okinawa governor now demands a review of the US forces pact. This case has reignited debate over the military presence on the island. A US Marine was indicted on suspicion of murdering a 39-year-old Japanese woman at a hotel in Okinawa - in a case that triggered outrage and reignited controversy over the US military presence on the island.

articles.title: Trump teases ‘big, beautiful agreement’ on Ukraine war and more
articles.summary: Donald Trump met with Kirill Dmitriev, a Russian special representative, on November 5. Dmitriev heads the Russian delegation for a Melania Trump event. The US president teased a significant agreement regarding the Ukraine war. The meeting was unscheduled and took place in Washington. US President Donald Trump held an unscheduled meeting on Thursday, November 5, with Kirill Dmitriev, a special representative of Russian President Vladimir Putin.

articles.title: Rubio says Trump's war against Iran not 'necessarily popular' but needed to stop a nuclear threat
articles.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended the ongoing war against Iran. He stated the conflict is necessary to stop a nuclear threat. Rubio acknowledged the war is not necessarily popular with voters. Many Americans blame Trump policies for higher energy prices and economic strain. America's top diplomat offered a robust defence of the more than eight-month-old war even as voters blamed Mr.

articles.title: China’s a green-tech superpower, but not yet a green civilization
articles.summary: China dominates global clean-tech production at the Antalya climate conference. The country manufactures most of the world's solar panels and batteries. Its emissions have stopped rising. However, experts argue it has not yet become a fully green civilization. At the UN climate conference in Antalya, which runs from November 9 to 20, China is the world’s clean-technology superpower. It makes most of the planet’s solar panels, batteries and electric vehicles.

articles.title: Pope Leo delivers stinging rebuke of Milei’s austerity measures during Argentina visit
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV criticized Javier Milei's austerity measures in Buenos Aires. The pontiff insisted the economy must serve the people. He delivered the speech during a 12-day Latin America tour. The audience in Argentina responded with rapturous applause to the critique. Pontiff tells Argentina’s president the economy must benefit all on second stop of 12-day Latin America tourPope Leo XIV has delivered a stinging critique of Argentine president Javier Milei’s harsh austerity measures, insisting growth must benefit all in a speech met with rapturous applause in Buenos Aires.“The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service.

articles.title: Pope Leo takes Milei to task as he visits divided Argentina
articles.summary: Pope Leo XVI criticized Argentine President Javier Milei during a visit to the divided nation. The pontiff defended the poor and pensioners, urging particular concern for those affected by illness, dependency, and disability. This statement served as a veiled rebuke of the government's controversial cuts to disability assistance. The remarks highlighted the growing friction between the Vatican and Milei's administration over social welfare policies.

articles.title: Ukraine Battles To Restore Power After Russian Attacks, As Trump Hints At Potential Territorial
articles.summary: Ukrainian crews worked to restore electricity to hundreds of thousands in the east after Russian airstrikes. Officials confirmed external power reached the Zaporizhzhya nuclear plant. Russian forces currently occupy that facility. Ukrainian authorities battled to restore power to hundreds of thousands of people in the east of the country following Russian air strikes, while officials said external power had been restored to the Zaporizhzhya nuclear plant, which is currently occupied by Russian forces.

articles.title: Pope’s visit to Argentina sets up showdown with ‘hyper-capitalist’ Milei
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrives in Argentina on 9 November for a visit that will test his relationship with President Javier Milei. The two men hold sharply opposing views on social and economic policy. Milei previously called the Pope's predecessor the representative of the Evil One. President has opposing views on many issues, and once called Leo’s predecessor the ‘representative of the Evil One’Trees are being planted in the garden.

articles.title: Uyghurs facing deportation by Thailand say they will be ‘like slaves’ in China
articles.summary: Activists warn that Thailand is preparing to deport more Uyghurs to China despite documented torture and abuse. One man said he would be like a slave if returned. Thai authorities forcibly deported 40 Uyghurs last year under pressure from Beijing. Activists fear Bangkok will give in to pressure from Beijing despite reports of torture and human rights abuses against the mostly muslim ethnic minorityThe deportation of two more Uyghurs to China from Thailand would put their lives in grave danger, activists have said, with one of the men saying he would be “like a slave” if he was sent back. Last year, Thai authorities forcibly deported 40 Uyghu.

articles.title: New Zealand faces weeks of uncertainty with results ‘too close to call’
articles.summary: New Zealand's National Party leads parliament, but no coalition has secured a majority. The country faces weeks of negotiations to form a government. Neither the right-wing bloc nor the left-wing opposition won a decisive mandate. National party will be largest in parliament but ultimate shape of next government won’t be settled for some timeNew Zealand could be facing a weeks-long wait to know the shape of its next government, after its nail-biting election failed to hand a decisive victory to either the incumbent rightwing coalition or opposition left bloc. articles.title: New Zealand election coalition talks will likely take weeks – as it happened
articles.summary: New Zealand's 2026 election is heading toward a hung parliament. National and Labour are neck and neck with eight percent of the vote counted. Minor parties hold the balance of power. No single party is expected to secure a majority. Polls show no coalition is expected to secure a majority of seats, in one of the closest elections in recent historyNew Zealand heads for election cliffhanger with minor party cast as kingmakerIn New Zealand’s bellwether seat, what are locals thinking as a knife-edge poll looms? Another update here with 8% of the vote counted.

articles.title: ‘For the first time I have my own chair’: Gaza siblings find new freedom
articles.summary: Ten-year-old Anas, born without legs and with limited hand function, received his first wheelchair in Gaza. He is one of three siblings who previously struggled to move or eat independently. The chair allows them to perform daily tasks with new freedom. In Gaza, 10-year-old Anas is one of three siblings born without legs and with only two fingers on each of their hands.

articles.title: Trump’s hubris more comedy than tragedy but echoes Greek original
articles.summary: Political analysts compare Donald Trump's recent actions to the Greek concept of hubris. They argue his excessive self-confidence mirrors historical patterns of destructive arrogance. This trend reflects a failure to accurately assess America's global power. Recently across the globe, political observers have likened the foibles and subsequent downfalls of presidents of the United States to hubris, the ancient Greek concept of destructive arrogance.

articles.title: Zelenskyy Says Russia Seeks Blackout In Ukraine Ahead Of US-Mediated Talks In Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: Russia launched 172 drones and 36 missiles at Kyiv on November 7. The strikes damaged energy infrastructure, housing, and a major Dnipro River bridge. The attack occurred just before scheduled talks in Abu Dhabi. Kyiv faced widespread damage and disruptions to essential services on November 7 after Russia launched 172 attack drones and 36 ballistic missiles at the Ukrainian capital and other regions, striking energy infrastructure, residential housing, and a major bridge over the Dnipro River.

articles.title: Japan, Taiwan, China and the emerging 2028 strategic test
articles.summary: East Asia is shifting toward a 2028 strategic test. Military, economic, and technological factors now intertwine. This convergence is reshaping regional order assumptions. The timing and drivers of this shift are changing. Originally published by Pacific Forum, this article is republished with permission. East Asia is entering an era in which military balance, economic resilience, technological leadership and alliance politics are no longer separate policy domains but interconnected elements of a broader contest over regional order.

articles.title: Here’s why Pyongyang is testing an array of missile capabilities
articles.summary: North Korea has conducted roughly 20 missile tests since early 2026. This marks a new phase in its development program. The focus is on capability breadth rather than launch volume. These tests signal a consequential shift in regional security dynamics. North Korea’s accelerating missile development has entered a new and potentially consequential phase. According to media reports available as of November 6, 2026, Pyongyang has conducted approximately 20 missile-related tests and exercises since the beginning of the year.

articles.title: Global stocks fall amid ‘big worries over AI’ after Democrats’ midterms triumph
articles.summary: Global stock markets plunged as investors feared an AI slowdown following the Democratic midterm victory. Asian and European indices mirrored Wall Street’s sharp decline. The FTSE dropped 1.9 percent on Friday. Tech shares led the sell-off across multiple regions. Asian and European markets follow Wall Street with sharp fall as FTSE is down 1.9%Business live – latest updatesEuropean stock markets have fallen sharply as a rout in US tech stocks spread across the Atlantic, after the Democrats’ midterms victory sparked fears of a slowdown in the AI industry. A sell-off on Wall Street on Thursday was followed by sharp falls in Asian stocks markets on Friday.

articles.title: Iran's Isolation Closes Doors For Young People Hoping To Build A Future Abroad
articles.summary: US and British English testing services have suspended operations in Iran. This move blocks a critical pathway for young Iranians seeking to study abroad. Sanctions and growing isolation continue to restrict their options for international education. Sanctions and growing international isolation are cutting key pathways for young Iranians with dreams of studying abroad. US and British English language-testing services have been suspended in Iran, creating another obstacle for prospective international students.

articles.title: Afghanistan faces deepening humanitarian crisis amid sweeping rights restrictions
articles.summary: A senior UN official called Afghanistan a difficult crossroad. The country faces a fragile economy and rights curbs. Humanitarian needs are acute five years after the Taliban returned. Stability is being undercut by these deepening restrictions. Afghanistan stands at a “difficult crossroad” more than five years after the Taliban returned to power, a senior UN official said on Friday. Relative stability and security are being undercut by a fragile economy, sweeping curbs on rights and acute humanitarian need.

articles.title: From a ship frozen into Arctic ice, a warning to world leaders: Trust the science
articles.summary: Scientists aboard a ship frozen in Arctic ice are documenting rapid environmental changes. They warn world leaders to trust climate science as sea ice retreats. Oil tankers are increasingly operating in the region, heightening the stakes for polar governance. Drifting through the polar darkness, a team of scientists is documenting a rapidly changing Arctic. As sea ice retreats and oil tankers move in, a conversation with the UN chief reveals why the battle for climate science matters far beyond the North Pole.

articles.title: ‘No Escape’ for refugees on the frontlines of the climate crisis
articles.summary: Nearly 90 million refugees live in countries facing high climate hazard exposure. Three in four displaced people face drought, floods, or extreme heat. This makes the climate emergency an immediate crisis for displaced populations. They have limited options for safe relocation. The climate emergency is an immediate crisis for refugees, with three in four – nearly 90 million people – living in countries facing high to severe exposure to hazards such as drought, floods and extreme heat.

articles.title: Deadly drone strikes mark ‘new and concerning’ threat, UN peacekeeping chief warns
articles.summary: UN peacekeeping chief warned the Security Council that drone strikes in Abyei pose a new threat. At least 30 people died in the attacks last month. The strikes added a concerning dimension to security in the disputed region. Drone strikes that killed at least 30 people in Abyei last month have added “a new and concerning dimension” to security in the disputed area, the UN’s peacekeeping chief told the Security Council on Thursday.

articles.title: What’s at stake at this year’s UN climate summit?
articles.summary: COP31 focuses on making advanced clean energy technologies affordable for all nations. The primary challenge is no longer finding solutions. The summit addresses the gap between technological availability and the financial capacity of millions to access these tools. The world has more tools than ever to tackle climate change, yet millions remain unable to benefit from them. As clean energy technologies advance faster than ever, the challenge facing countries at COP31 is no longer just finding solutions – but making sure everyone can afford them.

articles.title: Gunfire damages tents at Rafah displacement site in Gaza, as aid teams prepare for winter storms
articles.summary: Gunfire damaged multiple tents at a displacement site in northern Rafah on Tuesday. The United Nations reported that the incident caused injuries and forced a humanitarian partner to leave the area. Aid teams are now preparing for incoming winter storms in the region. Gunfire hit and damaged multiple tents at a displacement site in Gaza’s northern Rafah region on Tuesday, reportedly causing injuries and forcing a humanitarian partner to leave the area, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) has said.

articles.title: The View from Eritrea
articles.summary: Reuters journalist Giulia Paravicini discussed her recent reporting trip to Asmara, the capital of Eritrea. She detailed life in the isolated nation and its leadership's strategic calculations. The conversation covered mounting regional tensions and the country's complex relationship with neighboring Ethiopia. This week on The Horn, Alan speaks with Reuters journalist Giulia Paravicini about her recent reporting trip to Eritrea’s capital, Asmara, what she learned about life in the isolated country and its leadership’s calculations amid regional turmoil and mounting tensions with Ethiopia.

articles.summary: ट्रंप ने CBS इंटरव्यू में कहा कि जेलेंस्की और पुतिन की दुश्मनी शांति की सबसे बड़ी बाधा है। उन्होंने युद्ध के जल्दी समाधान की उम्मीद जताई। Trump Ukraine Statement: अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप ने इस बात पर काफी उम्मीद जताई है कि रूस-यूक्रेन युद्ध का समाधान जल्द ही निकल सकता है। उन्होंने कहा कि यूक्रेन के राष्ट्रपति वोलोदिमीर जेलेंस्की और रूस के राष्ट्रपति व्लादिमीर पुतिन के बीच की गहरी दुश्मनी ही शांति प्रयासों में सबसे बड़ी रुकावट है। CBS न्यूज को दिए एक विस्तृत इंटरव्यू में, अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति से पूछा गया कि उनके हिसाब से इस संघ।

articles.summary: ट्रंप ने 60 Minutes में कहा कि वह धार्मिक व्यक्ति हैं और सिद्धांत रूप में स्वर्ग जाएंगे। उन्होंने नरक जाने से इनकार किया। Trump Religious Beliefs: अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप ने एक न्यूज शो ’60 Minutes’ के एक इंटरव्यू के दौरान मृत्यु के बाद के जीवन और अपने धार्मिक विश्वासों पर खुलकर बात की।
